en: The northeast monsoon, called amihan, brings cool and dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
Soil around Mayon Volcano is highly fertile because volcanic ash adds essential minerals like potassium and phosphorus.
The underground rivers in Puerto Princesa flow through limestone caves formed by the dissolving action of slightly acidic rainwater.
Thick clouds often form over Mount Pulag when warm, moist air from the lowlands is forced upward by the mountain.
Venus appears as a brilliantly bright morning or evening star because its thick cloud cover reflects most of the sunlight.
The three aligned stars of Orion's Belt, locally known as Balatik, are easily visible in the night sky from December to May.
During a full moon, the aligned gravitational pull of the sun and moon causes higher high tides on Philippine beaches.
The Valley Fault System is a visible crack in the earth that runs directly through several cities in Metro Manila.
Storm surges during typhoons cause abnormal seawater rise that visibly floods low-lying coastal towns in the Visayas and Bicol regions.
Rainbows appear in the sky opposite the sun when sunlight refracts and reflects inside spherical raindrops after a brief shower.
The famous white sand of Boracay beaches is composed of finely crushed coral fragments and quartz eroded from nearby rocks.
The Milky Way galaxy appears as a bright, cloudy band of light across the dark night sky in rural Philippine provinces.
